decisions.reason: The existing referral_earnings_attribute already requires NFT attributes to reflect awarded commissions, including randomly allocated no-referral commissions.

The source explicitly requires ticket visibility parity across referral-code and no-referral mints on both the leaderboard and NFT attributes; the existing state does not state that full surface-specific parity.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
At this point, we have completed 12 mints, so that should amount to 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**Even if no referral code is used, a ticket and commission are still issued**.

Currently, **when a code is used**, it is accurately reflected on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

If **no referral code is used**, the ticket and commission are assigned at random.
(B**ut they must still be reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I believe that since your most recent fix, the randomly assigned tickets from the last 2 mints have been reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
However, the missing tickets have not been backfilled.

The commissions from these purchases without a code are also still not reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot, you will see that I have an NFT showing 2 tickets but only 1 x $5 commission. That should not be possible because each ticket includes a $5 commission.

Also, in my leaderboard screenshot, only 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions are accounted for out of 12 total mints.
Whether or not a referral code is used, 12 mints should result in 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions.

value_updates.ticket_visibility_parity: Tickets from both referral-code and no-referral mints must be reflected on the leaderboard and in NFT attributes.

decisions.reason: The FAQ already states that no-referral mints allocate commissions and tickets randomly, and the source does not request a change to FAQ copy.
The source concerns ticket and commission accounting, not displayed referral counts.
Ticket and commission visibility parity does not change the rule governing public referral-count accuracy.
The reference to 12 completed mints is evidence used to calculate rewards, not a change to the rule for displaying accurate mint statistics.
The source does not change which successfully minted NFTs must appear in a user's dashboard inventory.
Commission and ticket attribute visibility does not alter NFT image or media-rendering behavior.
The source does not change the prize amount, draw interval, countdown measure, or countdown display text.
The source addresses issued reward counts and their visibility, not the displayed prize-pool balance.
The About-page copy already describes random allocation when no code is provided, and the source does not request revised About-page content.
The active requirement already mandates random allocation of a ticket when no referral code is used; the source reiterates that rule rather than changing it.
